releaseScope: Native Rust/GPUI application for Arch/Omarchy Linux x86_64
releaseState: Omuse 0.7.0 qualified source pre-release: photo/vector editing, image tracing, editable SVG and shared control polish; no public binary is attached and hardware gates remain open

statusDefinitions.label: Locally tested
statusDefinitions.meaning: The named bounded journey passed on this development host. It is not a portability or universal quality claim.

statusDefinitions.label: Implemented / needs qualification
statusDefinitions.meaning: The source and UI path exist, but the current change or broader real-world claim still needs its final evidence.

statusDefinitions.label: Experimental
statusDefinitions.meaning: Available only through a bounded preview, explicit Try path, or provider-specific evidence.

statusDefinitions.label: Planned
statusDefinitions.meaning: Documented product direction without an implemented, qualified release path.

statusDefinitions.label: Blocked / deferred / excluded
statusDefinitions.meaning: Waiting on external evidence or deliberately outside the current preview scope.

releaseSnapshot.label: Editing update released
releaseSnapshot.detail: Implemented the OmaPhoto 1.3.3 editing backlog: Camera Raw gestures, text styling, imports, mask growth, effects, numeric controls, recent projects and save/reload safety. 1,105 application cases, exact-source CI, native journeys, compatibility and complete rollback passed.

releaseSnapshot.label: Photo/vector source release
releaseSnapshot.detail: Runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d includes the shared main canvas, precise Pen/Nodes gestures, local image tracing, editable single-path SVG, target-colour uniformity, high-quality sampling and shared 3-pixel control geometry. Local 1,206-case acceptance, exact-source CI, production/native journeys, installation and rollback passed. No public binary is attached.

releaseSnapshot.label: One project extension
releaseSnapshot.detail: .omuse for canvases, collections, pages/components and recovery. Legacy projects open without rewriting. Formats 1–11 are readable; ordinary canvas writes remain format 10 and vector-scene writes use format 11. 0.6 cannot read format-11 vector scenes or new target-colour-uniformity nodes. Save As retains older artwork; application rollback does not downgrade files. The 128×96 prior fixture decoded identically, two files stayed unchanged, and the old reader rejected format 11 without creating output.

releaseSnapshot.label: AI creation workflows
releaseSnapshot.value: Choose providers and finish a shared brief
releaseSnapshot.detail: Omuse 0.4.0 adds saved per-task provider choices, desktop subscription discovery fixes and optional image/edit → layout → caption sequences with one final reviewed Keep/Undo. Claude is text/layout only; Codex supports the visual/image paths. Grok and separately billed API routes remain unavailable.

releaseSnapshot.label: Numbered source release
releaseSnapshot.detail: Qualified numbered source runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d. The normal launcher selects this runtime; no public binary is attached.

releaseSnapshot.label: Current release regression suite
releaseSnapshot.detail: 494 library, 351 UI and 361 integration cases passed with zero failures and four ignored timing benchmarks. Editing/Create/media, 80 templates, four trace fixtures and save/recovery passed. Exact-source GitHub run 36910650216 completed successfully.

releaseSnapshot.label: Large-photo Create editing
releaseSnapshot.detail: Three paired desktop repetitions: paint core 85.69 → 0.32 ms; headless frame/refresh 257.88 → 165.38 ms. Recovery idle before each stroke; exact undo/redo/recovery, unchanged peak memory. Physical input latency remains unmeasured.

releaseSnapshot.label: Public-release blockers
releaseSnapshot.detail: No public binary is attached. Dependency notices, clean-machine and broader hardware/accessibility acceptance remain open. Runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d passed local and exact-source CI, 13 native/gallery journeys, installation and rollback.

categories.name: Photo editing
categories.summary: Ordinary raster work is broad and locally exercised; the active release pass is tightening real-photo colour, precision and scale evidence.

items.name: Core raster editing
items.current: Brush, Pencil, Eraser, Fill, Gradient, Crop, Resize, Move, Clone, Blur, Smudge, Liquify, Heal, Spot Heal and destructive filters are wired into the native editor with undo/redo. Moving rotated/reflected layers preserves their transforms; proportional resizing can cross its anchor, and corner distortion preserves pixel orientation without baking stationary clicks.
items.boundary: Bounded local journeys do not establish every brush size, transform, colour space or long-session workload.

items.name: Selections and selection-aware edits
items.current: Marquee, ellipse, lasso, wand, object selection, feathered coverage and selection-aware filters/content fill are implemented; the hardened paths preserve soft coverage and undo.
items.boundary: Quality still depends on the source and tool settings; physical input delivery is a separate desktop gate.

items.name: Retouching and controlled removal
items.current: Local Spot Healing, Clone/Healing, content-aware fill, healing layers, frequency separation and controlled removal are implemented. Final 189f3e7 Cua check removed a synthetic blemish with J, then with Ctrl+K Content-aware fill; each restored it with one Ctrl+Z. Engine tests cover exact selection/undo integrity and allowed sampling areas.
items.boundary: The manual explains local versus AI removal and limits. Controlled removal has a 4 MP input ceiling; ordinary fill is bounded to 16,777,216 source pixels and 250,000 selected pixels. Synthetic checks do not establish complex photographic reconstruction quality.

items.name: Adjustments, filters and editable stacks
items.current: Exposure, levels, curves, hue/saturation, colour balance, blur, sharpen, denoise, grain/noise, vignette, bloom, tonal contrast, invert and grayscale are available through destructive and editable paths.
items.boundary: The Camera Raw compatibility node remains an 8-bit path; not every traditional adjustment/effect can be exported at full precision.

items.name: Camera Raw scopes and preview responsiveness
items.current: RGB histogram and hue/saturation vectorscope use bounded alpha-weighted samples. Camera Raw adds stage-aware neutral white-balance and defringe sampling, targeted curve/HSL drags, and one active plus one newest queued preview. Cancelled and stale work cannot replace another document or dialog.
items.boundary: Six numerical gesture cases, four GUI gesture cases and lifecycle checks pass within the release suite. Full-resolution 8-bit grading is limited to 16 MP; canvas references are bounded. Scopes/samplers describe display RGB, not sensor RAW/HDR; no comparative speed claim.

items.name: Embedded RAW development
items.current: LibRaw import retains original bytes and a 16-bit editable source. After visual review rejected a grossly magenta result, the corrected Nikon and Canon outputs both match the independent C++ camera-white-balance PPM16 references exactly for every retained sample and were visually inspected as natural.
items.boundary: The earlier two-camera evidence uses the same pinned LibRaw engine, not an independent audit of LibRaw colour science or a general camera-colour claim. The earlier 734-test suite passed with the Nikon RAW fixture enabled; the full 16-case corpus was not repeated for the history/ownership or photo-integrity changes.

items.name: Real-photo and large-document qualification
items.current: The 16 photo cases passed at ac8874d. The isolated region-history workload at a69a5f6 passed 18 runs with 100 strokes, exact final undo/redo pixels, .omuse save/reopen and PNG export; routine medians were 2.00/2.13/0.42 ms at 12/24/48 MP. The later desktop ownership comparison is recorded separately below.
items.boundary: The earlier isolated editor fixture measured median peak RSS of 326/610/1200 MiB and does not establish physical input latency. The later desktop fixture also waits for recovery before painting. Rapid strokes during background work, native large-camera decode and long sessions still need qualification.

items.name: Region/tile-based large-photo history
items.current: Large unselected Brush, Pencil and Eraser strokes retain reversible 256×256 tiles. Current differential regressions pass. Historical a69a5f6 measurements retained 100 undo steps at 48 MP using about 30.96 MiB of final history, compared with one step before.
items.boundary: Masks, selected strokes, clone/heal and other transactions keep snapshots. Persistent Create raster owners are now removed, but recovery, collection checkpoints and saves can still force copies. The earlier 12/24 MP first strokes were slower; neither workload qualifies whole-app input latency.

items.name: Large-photo desktop page ownership
items.current: Editors own active and cached page pixels; complete save/export/recovery snapshots remain frozen. All 18 paired cases passed. At 48 MP, paint core measured 85.69 → 0.32 ms and headless frame/refresh 257.88 → 165.38 ms. Editing during a same-path save can recover, export and save again.
items.boundary: Twelve localized strokes after a warmup, three repetitions per strategy/size; recovery idle before each measured stroke. Peak RSS was essentially unchanged. In-flight snapshots can still force full copies, and end-of-stroke refresh has large outliers. These are not physical input timings.

items.name: Interactive crop and photo/social ratios
items.current: Crop opens a movable frame seeded from the selection or full canvas. Free, Original, 1:1, 4:5, 3:2 and 16:9 presets, orientation swap, corner resizing, arrow nudging and Apply/Cancel are implemented. Original pixels remain in their layers; Apply is one undo step.
items.boundary: Automated/native/Cua checks passed on 0.3.0. Integer output can round a ratio by one pixel; crop rotation and perspective correction are separate tools.

items.name: Responsive outlines for complex selections
items.current: Zoom-aware background outlines, visible-region clipping, cancellation and a 65,536-point display cap. Exact selection pixels remain unchanged.
items.boundary: Contour, selection-generation and combined UI regressions passed. One immutable selection snapshot is copied per generation. Exact masks remain unchanged; no comparative speed measurement.

items.name: Dither, halftone and retro image effects
items.current: Ten deterministic Dither styles plus Bloom Glow, Vignette Overlay and Local Contrast. The finishing panel previews, applies cached exact pixels and supports selection-aware Undo.
items.boundary: Engine, Apply/Undo, selection and lower-controls scrolling/typing regressions passed. Production Dither/Bloom/Vignette panels were inspected in dark/light themes. Requires 8-bit raster copies and canvases/layers up to 16 MP; retained masters stay unchanged.

items.name: Smudge trail and Liquify sharpness follow-up
items.current: Source review found the older carried-colour Smudge algorithm and repeated per-dab Liquify resampling in the current release. Recommended next work: reproduce fading-dot trails and forward/back line-art/photo cases, then evaluate revised Smudge spacing/carry and a bounded CPU displacement-field Liquify.
items.boundary: No quality regression has been independently measured in this watch and no fix is shipped. Preserve soft selections, alpha, placement, cancellation and exact Undo. Denser dabs and offset fields need explicit work/memory budgets and timings. Upstream GPU measurements are not Omuse results.

items.name: Camera Raw curve semantics and graph refinement
items.current: Compare smoother parametric bends and an RGB master curve against the existing luminance-first recipe. Point dragging already preserves its captured point and order; region/divider gestures and a selected-point readout are proposed refinements.
items.boundary: Changing curve or Refine Saturation meaning needs explicit recipe/version compatibility so existing saved grades keep their appearance. Add independent reference pixels and gesture regressions first; this is not Photoshop colour certification or a shipped 0.6.0 change.

items.name: Scanlines and CRT finishing
items.current: A distinct Scanlines/CRT finish is a candidate addition identified in the new upstream roadmap. Current Omuse Dither exposes ten existing styles, including halftone lines and ASCII.
items.boundary: Halftone lines are not a separate CRT mode. No new effect was implemented or qualified in this review; preview/Apply, selection, transparency, cancellation and Undo would need coverage.

items.name: Complete photo precision and export fidelity
items.current: Approved P01/P02: the development branch passed bounded sampling, alpha/mask and cancellation checks for the new 16-bit renderer. Removing the Camera Raw 8-bit bottleneck and extending full-precision effects remain planned.
items.boundary: Installed/public 0.6.0 is unchanged. Reduced masked detail can still differ between the 8-bit canvas and 16-bit export. Complete high-precision editing and independent photographic quality remain unqualified.

items.name: Measured camera and lens profiles
items.current: Approved P03: camera/lens identification, compatible calibrated profiles, manual overrides and independently reviewed colour-chart/correction cases.
items.boundary: Current generic correction controls are not a measured camera/lens profile database. Camera support, profile licensing and real-input quality remain work.

items.name: Reference-look matching and campaign colour
items.current: Approved P06/P12: editable reference-look matching and consistent product/campaign recipes, building on the new development target-colour node.
items.boundary: Preserve texture, alpha and high-bit-depth data. Reference matching must return reviewable adjustments; no quality or cross-photo consistency is yet qualified.

items.name: Detail-preserving restoration and enlargement
items.current: Approved P08: learned denoise, deblur, enlargement and optional scratch/face/text recovery, with detail comparison and retained originals.
items.boundary: Current local restoration uses conventional filtering/resizing. Model availability, licence, Linux execution, generated-detail behaviour and resource cost require evidence before integration.

items.name: Depth masks and editable relighting
items.current: Approved P09/P12: editable depth masks, separate near/far brightness and warmth, portrait/product relighting and edge/halo correction.
items.boundary: No current depth-based relighting implementation. Depth estimates and difficult hair/transparency need correction controls and independent image review.

items.name: Robust, re-editable multi-image merges
items.current: Approved P10: rotation/perspective registration, panorama projection, focus-blend improvements, HDR moving-subject handling and retained merge recipes.
items.boundary: Current merges are translation-only, bounded to 16 MP output and normalize HDR into 16-bit linear sRGB; no persistent 32-bit radiance or editable merge history.

items.name: Target colour uniformity — 0.7.0
items.current: Omuse 0.7.0 runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d provides an editable Filter stack node with a reference colour, circular hue range/falloff and independent hue/saturation/lightness strengths. Native 16-bit evaluation, alpha, node opacity and selection masks are retained.
items.boundary: Encoded-sRGB HSL, not semantic skin selection or reference-look matching. Selected P3 colours use bounded sRGB semantics. Unaffected native samples are preserved. A project containing this new node requires the 0.7.0 reader; retain a 0.6-compatible copy with Save As. See docs/release-070-qualification.md.

categories.name: Layers and masks
categories.summary: The native document model covers hierarchy, editable effects and multiple mask types with bounded persistence and transaction tests.

items.name: Layer hierarchy and compositing
items.current: Pixel layers, groups, transforms, opacity, blend modes, clipping, visibility, locking, reorder/copy and grouped editing are implemented. Clipped groups retain independent live-mask links on descendant layers in both renderers.
items.boundary: Cross-window layer drops and complete parity with every legacy Mac gesture remain outside the current evidence.

items.name: Raster, linked and folder masks
items.current: Per-layer masks, detached placement, link/unlink behavior, live alpha links and folder masks persist through project save/reopen.
items.boundary: Mask growth is implemented in the separate 0.6.0 growing-masks card. Rasterization and document limits remain bounded; older project versions cannot represent every newer mask feature.

items.name: Adjustment layers and layer effects
items.current: Hue/Saturation, Levels, Curves, Exposure, Gradient Map and Grain adjustment records coexist with stroke, shadows, colour overlay and outer glow effects.
items.boundary: Legacy-reader support varies by project version, and 16-bit export rejects unsupported traditional adjustment/effect records rather than flattening silently.

items.name: Editable filter stacks and Blend If
items.current: Retained sources support ordered filter nodes, opacity, selection masks and backdrop-aware Blend If with channel controls.
items.boundary: Editable layers are capped at 128 nodes; source and mask storage budgets apply, and evaluation remains CPU-heavy for large images.

items.name: Range masks and edge refinement
items.current: Luminosity/colour ranges can replace, add or subtract selections or produce layer masks; refinement supports correction strokes, edge controls and multiple inspection backgrounds.
items.boundary: Range parameters are not persisted as a live parametric mask recipe, and refined cut-outs bake the correction result.

items.name: Vector masks
items.current: Cubic path geometry remains editable while its vector mask is rasterized into layer coverage; path Apply rebuilds that coverage transactionally.
items.boundary: This is a bounded path/mask workflow, not compound-path boolean authoring or a complete vector illustration system.

items.name: Editable layer clipboard and Linux image exchange
items.current: Copy without a pixel selection retains complete selected trees, masks, transforms, locks and advanced sources in the running Omuse session. Paste remaps internal identities and commits once. Native Wayland and XWayland PNG exchange preserved exact source pixels. Bounded nonblocking writes keep the UI responsive to slow readers; delayed pastes reject stale state and active interactions. Unsafe or no-op pixel/mask cuts preserve the previous clipboard.
items.boundary: Payload is capped at 256 MiB and the full-resolution PNG at a 16 MP source canvas. Missing mask dependencies reject. Separate processes, clipboard managers and app restarts do not carry editable trees. An idle reader can retain its transfer buffer until it closes.

items.name: Paint masks beyond their original bounds
items.current: Brush, fill and gradient masks can grow while preserving placement, linked/detached geometry, outside coverage and original layer pixels.
items.boundary: New and existing mask regressions passed in the combined suite. Expansion has a 16 MP interactive cap with failure rollback. Outside coverage and grown folder-mask placement require canvas format 10.

items.name: Persistent range, refinement and semantic masks
items.current: Approved P04: retain mask recipes/correction strokes; select person, hair, clothing and face regions, then add/subtract/intersect and refine manually.
items.boundary: Existing selection/refinement results do not establish complete semantic masking or retained correction histories. Qualify varied real subjects and preserve source pixels.

categories.name: Vector, type and design
categories.summary: Live type, shape and layout objects now support native branded design while preserving an explicit boundary around full illustration tooling.

items.name: Live text and rich typography
items.current: Editable text supports rich runs, alignment, fitting, reusable styles and overflow reports. Omuse 0.6.0 renders drafts through the artwork pipeline with masks/effects and selected-letter colour edits; Rich Typography supplies per-range font and size overrides.
items.boundary: Direct inline font changes for a highlighted selection with mixed-style feedback remain a proposed improvement. Unusual fonts, native IME and assistive workflows retain their separate qualification limits.

items.name: Live shapes and paths
items.current: Rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, lines and editable cubic paths retain style/geometry. The native path editor adds/moves anchors and handles, smooths nodes and creates vector masks, with Apply/Undo, styling and persistence regressions.
items.boundary: This is a bounded path editor, not full Photoshop-style direct canvas pen-tool parity. Boolean operations and variable-width strokes remain outside the general illustration feature set.

items.name: Frames and collages
items.current: Replaceable image frames retain crop placement, focal point, rounded boundary and nondestructive replacement metadata.
items.boundary: Frame/cutout visual quality across arbitrary source photography remains a manual review area.

items.name: Brand kits and editable templates
items.current: Brand colours, logos, font pairs, text styles and spacing rules feed 20 native templates and 80 qualified variants.
items.boundary: The completed variants are bounded fixtures; arbitrary user brands and missing-font substitutions require manual review.

items.name: Responsive layout and resizing
items.current: Alignment, distribution, anchoring and aspect-ratio adaptation retain live text/shapes and editable overrides.
items.boundary: Layout preflight is conservative and does not judge every image backdrop, rich text run or destination safe area.

items.name: Reusable components and shared backgrounds
items.current: Reusable logos, badges, footers and calls to action support bounded instance overrides and explicit propagation across pages.
items.boundary: Components are project-native structures, not a remote collaborative design-system service.

items.name: Mesh and pin deformation
items.current: A retained 2×2 corner mesh and bounded pin warp can be previewed, applied, reopened and adjusted.
items.boundary: The UI is not a general mesh-grid editor; evaluation is CPU-based and capped at 16 MP.

items.name: Live canvas text and effects while typing
items.current: Background draft rendering uses the committed text/compositing path. Select actual letters to colour them, retain styles during Unicode typing, and Apply as one document Undo.
items.boundary: Preview/Apply pixels, placed masks/rotation/blend, picker cancellation/focus, stale jobs and Unicode typing/Undo regressions passed. Native IME and broad font coverage remain separate evidence gaps.

items.name: Direct canvas Pen and Node workflow
items.current: Approved V01: canvas path editing, node insertion/split/join, corner/smooth controls and snapping/nudging. First improve the current draft editor alongside SVG path exchange.
items.boundary: The existing bounded dialog is not a complete direct-canvas tool. Every gesture needs one reversible transaction, cancellation and keyboard coverage.

items.name: Shape Builder and compound geometry
items.current: Approved V02: union, subtraction, intersection, exclusion/division and compound-path authoring with a visual construction tool.
items.boundary: Not implemented. Holes, tangencies, self-intersections, fill rules and degenerate geometry require independent correctness and workload tests.

items.name: Advanced editable vector strokes and fills
items.current: Approved V03/V08: gradients, caps/joins/dashes, variable-width strokes, stroke expansion, offsets, corners and later mesh/pattern fills, repeats and blends.
items.boundary: Retained paths currently expose solid fill and uniform stroke. Broader illustration operations require versioned persistence and explicit complexity budgets.

items.name: Path typography and text outlines
items.current: Approved V04: text on a path, outline copies retaining original text, improved per-selection inline styling and clear font fallback reporting.
items.boundary: Unusual fonts, non-Latin shaping, native IME and exported font fidelity require qualification. Current editable text is not outlined/path typography.

items.name: Editable logo and sketch tracing
items.current: Approved V05: preview bitmap-to-vector results with palette, detail and smoothing controls, node counts and retained original artwork.
items.boundary: Not implemented. Bound tracing complexity and do not promise lossless photographic reconstruction; independently review logo and line-art fixtures.

items.name: Compound-path and node controls — 0.7.0
items.current: Omuse 0.7.0 runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d provides corner/smooth nodes, exact curve midpoint insertion, reverse/new subpaths, open/close and even-odd/non-zero fills. Preview compound holes correctly; Apply is one Undo step.
items.boundary: Legacy retained-path/mask dialogs remain available for compatibility. Modern scene paths use the main canvas. Split/join, snapping, booleans and variable-width strokes remain on the roadmap.

items.name: Multiple editable objects in one artwork layer — 0.7.0
items.current: The procedural engine checkpoint at source 4e1da33 passed optimized regressions, both native backends, 4K save/reopen/export and old-reader refusal. Several objects share one retained geometry scene and derived RGBA8 cache. The new unified canvas interaction layer is tracked separately below.
items.boundary: Format 11 requires the 0.7.0 reader; ordinary canvases stay format 10. Geometry/cache digests and cumulative expansion budgets are enforced. Pixel edits require explicit Rasterize. Persistent visible-tile caches, multi-object SVG and 16-bit procedural rendering remain open. Historical storage accounting is not process RSS or rendering speed. See docs/release-070-qualification.md.

items.name: Photo and vector editing on one canvas — 0.7.0
items.current: Omuse 0.7.0 runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d provides the shared main canvas, compact Layers inspector, on-canvas object picking, transformed node/handle dragging, P/A/V tools, double-click node editing in Move mode, live styles, bounded local Undo/Redo, and one document transaction when finished. Tool/layer/save changes retain valid edits automatically. Space, middle-drag, scroll zoom, command search and shortcut help stay integrated.
items.boundary: Previews use a coalesced full-document compositor; instant full-resolution recomposition and broad hardware/latency claims remain unqualified. Format-11 requirements remain; 0.6 cannot read vector scenes. Release evidence is recorded in docs/release-070-qualification.md.

items.name: Image tracing and precise curve gestures — 0.7.0
items.current: Omuse 0.7.0 runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d provides local bitmap-to-vector tracing in the main canvas/inspector with Logo, Illustration and Photo presets, Colour/Gray/B&W, detail/smoothing/corners/noise/resolution/point budgets, Source/Trace comparison, retained bitmap, saved settings/retrace and one Undo transaction. Pen click-drag creates smooth curves; A moves points/handles; Alt frees handles, Shift constrains angles, and segment insertion preserves the curve.
items.boundary: Four independently sampled synthetic tracing fixtures passed; one logo fixture reduced 476 linear anchors to 20 curved anchors (95.8%). This is not an arbitrary-photo guarantee. 16 MP source, 4 MP working and explicit work/geometry budgets. RGBA8 solid-colour approximation with a source-resolution display cache. Complete SVG export, broad photo fidelity, pathological topology, large-document latency and Illustrator parity remain unqualified. See docs/release-070-qualification.md.

categories.name: Create and social content
categories.summary: Create is implemented as a native content-production workspace for editable assets and export, without scheduling or social account management.

items.name: Pages, artboards and carousels
items.current: `.omuse` collections support mixed page sizes, page strips, reorder/duplicate, shared backgrounds, numbering and collection undo/redo. New and duplicate pages reject invalid dimensions, names and aggregate canvas overflow before changing or loading the collection.
items.boundary: Older application builds may not understand Create metadata; keep the full collection package intact.

items.name: Phone preview, guides and content packs
items.current: Phone preview, composition guides and staged export produce ordered PNG/JPEG/WebP pages, multipage PDF, captions, alt text and a manifest.
items.boundary: Safe-area guidance is conservative; destination applications can crop or overlay content differently.

items.name: CSV bulk creation
items.current: CSV rows bind typed text, image, visibility and alt fields to approved templates with validation, preview and meaningful output names.
items.boundary: A representative user batch, row-error presentation and final naming review remain manual acceptance work.

items.name: Local asset library
items.current: Local photos, cutouts, logos, backgrounds and saved compositions can be searched, tagged, favourited and packaged into projects with provenance.
items.boundary: This is a local library; cloud sync and collaborative asset governance are not claimed.

items.name: Motion and animated output
items.current: Page/layer fades, rise, slow pan, durations, transitions and local MP4/GIF export are implemented through FFmpeg.
items.boundary: FFmpeg availability and user-media compatibility remain host-dependent; a saved assistant animation plan was not separately rendered in its live AI journey.

items.name: Short clips, audio and subtitles
items.current: Supplied clips can be probed, trimmed and split; projects retain audio settings and editable SRT/WebVTT cues for soft or burned subtitles.
items.boundary: Cancellation, unusual codecs and a broad user-media matrix remain release checks.

items.name: Automatic transcription
items.current: Subtitle import and editing exist; automatic transcription is documented as a future, separately qualified capability.
items.boundary: There is no current transcription runtime or release claim.

items.name: Calendars, scheduling and publishing
items.current: Explicitly excluded from Omuse's product scope. Content sets may have names, briefs and versions without dates, publishing states or analytics.
items.boundary: This is an exclusion, not an unfinished preview promise.

categories.name: AI
categories.summary: Task-based creation with per-task subscription choices, optional bounded follow-on steps and one reviewed editable result. Provider capability and live quality remain operation-specific.

items.name: Ask Omuse job, review and history model
items.current: Ask Omuse has eight task choices, editable starter briefs, one task-aware submit action, explicit request context, compact Connections/history, Before/After review, caption copying and refinement carrying the previous plan. Photo/caption task contracts reject empty or out-of-scope results. Provider frames are preserved across acknowledgements; discovery is parallel, bounded and cancellable. History merges concurrent writes transactionally and respects serialized metadata budgets.
items.boundary: Runtime 3dc3e46 passed 843 application tests, full remote CI and 24 production Wayland, 24 XWayland and 24 installed Wayland checks. Exact-final Cua verifies saved-history rejection on changed canvas, task-preserving refinement, readable layer names and Keep/Undo. Remote cancellation and broader account/image quality remain separate.

items.name: Per-task provider routing and follow-on sequences
items.current: Omuse 0.4.0 lets each of eight Ask Omuse tasks use Auto or a pinned provider, with preferred Assistant and Images roles plus Auto exclusions. Optional image/edit follow-ons run editable Design then Caption as a frozen sequence of at most three disclosed requests, one brief and one final review. Saved preferences migrate safely and replay preserves generated-layer identities.
items.boundary: 949 release cases cover routing, preflight, cancellation, source changes and replay. Pins never fall back and errors are not retried. Codex is required for visual Photo/Caption and images; Claude is text/layout only, Grok unqualified. Broader live failure/cancellation and output acceptance remain open.

items.name: Omarchy desktop subscription discovery
items.current: Omuse 0.4.0 safely resolves recognized Omarchy mise shims before checking provider identity, fixing false Unverified results after desktop launch. The earlier 3117032 discovery check reported Codex and Claude Code 2.1.283 Ready / SubscriptionAllowance; the normal launcher needs no temporary PATH workaround.
items.boundary: Runtime identity, account and isolation checks remain enforced. Arbitrary wrappers stay rejected. Earlier account probes retain their candidate and operation scope; a login does not qualify every task.

items.name: Codex subscription route
items.current: Codex CLI 0.158.0 passed five independent live Generate, Replace, Remove, Background and Expand requests on 9100ef4, one variation each without automatic retries. Review, Keep, save/reopen and Undo/Redo passed, with exact protected/translated pixels where applicable. Prior photo/caption/refinement receipts retain their 0.2.0 identities.
items.boundary: The final 189f3e7 changes only local finishing focus and UI coverage/selectors; it passed full CI and UI/native/Cua checks separately. Synthetic receipts do not qualify other accounts, prompts, provider versions, photographic quality or multi-variation cancellation.

items.name: Generate and image-edit operations
items.current: Generate, Replace, Remove, Background and Expand each passed a live Codex subscription journey on 9100ef4. Masked edits protected every excluded pixel; Expand preserved the original rectangle exactly. Locked clipping dependencies, adjustment-aware expansion, failed-history result lifetime and selection-aware review are covered. Final finishing focus repair qualified separately on 189f3e7.
items.boundary: Bounded 64×80 synthetic source, one variation and zero automatic retries per intent. Multi-variation cancellation, longer refinement/failure/restart and representative photographic outcomes remain open. Claude/Grok require separate operation evidence.

items.name: Native design assistant
items.current: Design with me and Improve layout can propose bounded native plans that select pages, place packaged resources and instantiate components with overrides. In local public candidate 3117032, one installed Claude welcome-card request returned five editable operations; Cua verified Review, Keep, toolbar Undo and Redo.
items.boundary: Live design evidence covers the earlier named Codex journeys and one synthetic Claude Design request. The Claude demonstration was not saved or reopened; cancellation, refinement, follow-up, broader plans and design quality remain unqualified.

items.name: Reversible AI photo enhancement
items.current: Typed adjust_photo adds clipped editable Exposure, Curves and Hue/Saturation layers. Regressions verify target protection, original pixels, masks, save/reopen and Undo. categories.name: Formats and colour
categories.summary: Omuse preserves editable project state and common raster/media outputs while keeping colour and format limitations explicit.

items.name: `.omuse` canvases and legacy import
items.current: Single canvases and collections use .omuse. Canvases read formats 1–10 and write format 10; Unicode colour runs are validated. Legacy .comp opens without rewriting and first Save offers an .omuse copy. Existing destinations require confirmation.
items.boundary: Omuse 0.5 and earlier cannot read new format 10 saves. Previous production format 9 artwork rendered identically and its 7 source files were unchanged. Save As preserves older copies; app rollback does not downgrade files.

items.name: `.omuse` collections
items.current: Multi-page .omuse collections save schema v2 with nested .omuse pages and components. The reader accepts v1 collections with nested .comp packages, preserving lazy documents, resources, metadata and undo snapshots during migration.
items.boundary: Migration and prior-release reader checks passed. Saving a v1 collection upgrades it; Omuse 0.4.0 and earlier cannot read v2. Use Save As to preserve a v1 copy for older releases. Independent cross-app interchange remains a separate gate.

items.name: Raster import and export
items.current: PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP and common image import paths support orientation, tagged colour conversion, staged publication and explicit JPEG matte/quality behavior.
items.boundary: The 14 non-RAW corpus cases and current Rust/UI regressions pass, including warning-free TIFF alpha decoding. Broader format and clean-machine qualification remain separate.

items.name: PSD subset
items.current: Omuse 0.6.0 imports bounded 8-bit RGB PSD and PSB with supported groups, opacity/fill, masks, clipping and blend/adjustment mappings. Supported simple horizontal Photoshop text is editable with cached appearance retained until an actual text edit; unsupported text uses a reported raster fallback.
items.boundary: CMYK, 16/32-bit Photoshop documents and embedded ICC profiles are refused. Independent small Photoshop fixtures and constructed regressions passed in the 0.6.0 suite; full Photoshop/Affinity interchange and a broad image-quality corpus remain separate qualification work.

items.name: ICC and working spaces
items.current: ICC-tagged imports normalize through LittleCMS; editable sources can use sRGB, Linear sRGB or Display P3, and software display proofing exposes intents and black-point compensation.
items.boundary: End-to-end wide-gamut compositing/export, calibrated monitor validation, compositor colour management, HDR display and print-proof accuracy are unqualified.

items.name: Retained 16-bit precision and export
items.current: High-bit-depth PNG/TIFF and RAW sources retain non-quantized 16-bit masters for editable processing and explicit 16-bit PNG/TIFF export. Clipping stacks preserve base transparency, masks and Blend If; live-mask chains resolve independently of layer order and include source parent opacity.
items.boundary: Both RAW references and retained/explicit PNG/TIFF samples pass exact 16-bit comparison; high-precision sources remain capped at 16,777,216 pixels. Standard export is 8-bit, while explicit PNG/TIFF export is 16-bit. Ordinary destructive painting requires an explicit conversion to 8-bit pixels. Released 0.6.0 uses bilinear high-quality downsampling; the separate development sampling entry tracks its Lanczos replacement and remaining masked-preview differences.

items.name: Persistent 32-bit HDR workflow
items.current: Approved P11: persistent 32-bit radiance, explicit tone mapping and complete wide-gamut compositing/export remain planned; existing retained 16-bit sources and working-space conversions are foundations.
items.boundary: Existing HDR merge and P3 working-space features must not be described as a 32-bit floating-point HDR pipeline.

items.name: PSB, editable Photoshop text and SVG import
items.current: Bounded PSB and SVG/SVGZ import, selectable SVG raster size, supported editable TypeTool descriptors, cached fallback artwork and explicit conversion notes.
items.boundary: The combined suite passed real Photoshop alignment/cached-text fixtures, SVG source-change checks and bounded import regressions. Embedded-ICC Photoshop input remains an explicit refusal. SVG imports pixels, not editable vector trees; full interchange is not claimed.

items.name: OmaPhoto / Compositor format-10 import
items.current: Reads formats 1–10 and maps upstream UTF-16 colour runs to validated native UTF-8 rich text without rerendering cached artwork. New saves are .omuse canvas format 10.
items.boundary: Format-10 conversion, malformed range/version rejection, encoding ambiguity and mask-coverage regressions passed within the recorded 0.6.0 suite. Older readers reject new saves; use Save As to retain an older copy. These checks do not establish complete independently authored cross-app interchange.

items.name: Multi-object editable SVG documents
items.current: Approved V06 expansion beyond the new single-path route: multiple objects, hierarchy, transforms, text, gradients and supported clipping.
items.boundary: Requires the versioned procedural vector scene and bounded tile-cache checkpoint in Q01/Q02 before expansion. The development single-path importer is a separate bounded feature; general Open/Import rasterizes SVG. Full document round-trip is not implemented.

items.name: Vector PDF and bounded Illustrator interchange
items.current: Approved V07/V09: retain supported geometry/text in PDF, declare raster-effect fallbacks and font handling, then investigate PDF-compatible AI import.
items.boundary: Current multipage raster PDF is not vector-preserving PDF. Full proprietary Illustrator document round-trip remains a separate research item.

items.name: Qualified print colour and output
items.current: Approved Q05: separately develop and qualify CMYK, spot colours, overprint and print-proofing with suitable fixtures.
items.boundary: No press-readiness claim follows from adding vectors or PDF output. Monitor/compositor and print validation are independent of file parsing.

items.name: Editable SVG path exchange — 0.7.0
items.current: Omuse 0.7.0 runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d explicitly imports one styled path/basic shape, fits its viewport into a layer, edits its curves and exports editable SVG to a new file. Compound holes, fill/stroke opacity and supported transforms are retained.
items.boundary: 4 MiB and 100,000 anchors; single painted object only. Round uniform strokes; no text, photos, gradients, effects, resources or multiple objects. Export uses source coordinates, excluding composition effects and layer placement.

items.name: High-quality 16-bit sampling — 0.7.0
items.current: Omuse 0.7.0 runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d provides scale-aware premultiplied Lanczos for transformed retained 16-bit sources, with local/folder masks integrated in source taps. Identity samples remain exact, Smooth and Nearest stay explicit, and source promotion, conversion and sampling check cancellation.
items.boundary: A 66×66 footprint and 3/32 scale floor bound extreme reductions. Non-aligned nested masks can be expensive. The 8-bit canvas filters masks independently and may differ on reduced masked detail. No speed or complete colour-management claim.

items.name: Windows development build
items.current: The editor opens, edits, saves and reopens canvases and Create collections on Windows 11 x86_64 with MSVC, develops Camera RAW through LibRaw, selects subjects with local ONNX Runtime inference and exports MP4/GIF motion through FFmpeg on PATH. Settings use %APPDATA%\omuse; data, recovery and state use %LOCALAPPDATA%\omuse unless XDG variables are set. omuse.exe is a GUI-subsystem program with a static C runtime. scripts/prepare-rust-assets.ps1 fetches the pinned model and ONNX Runtime and builds LibRaw; scripts/package-rust.ps1 creates a zip with runtime assets, notices and a Windows dependency inventory. The windows CI job runs the test suite and the editing, Create, template catalog and motion journeys, then keeps the unsigned zip as a 14-day workflow artifact.
items.boundary: Not a release target and not qualified. On Windows 11 Pro the full suite passed with --test-threads=1 including real u2netp inference; the self-test, Create acceptance with motion, media acceptance, all 80 template variants and a Nikon D90 NEF photo journey (also from a Unicode path) passed, and the packaged build selected a subject in the native window. Windows has no atomic directory exchange: replacing a project moves the previous package to a hidden sibling between two renames. Subject selection needs the Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable for Microsoft's onnxruntime.dll; FFmpeg is not bundled. The zip is unsigned and four Windows dependency notice findings remain open. Ask Omuse, tablet pressure and Omarchy theme following are not available on Windows. No physical tablet, mixed-DPI, multi-monitor or clean-machine checks. Linux behaviour and project formats are unchanged.

categories.name: Reliability and release
categories.summary: Transaction, recovery and bounds work is substantial, while public distribution still depends on current qualification and external release infrastructure.

items.name: Undo, async work and publication safety
items.current: Document transactions, undo/redo, stale-result rejection, cancellable background open/export/save and staged publication guard against partial or late results.
items.boundary: Cancellation cannot retract work already accepted by an external provider, and not every long-running workload has soak evidence.

items.name: Save, recovery and interruption
items.current: Staged saves, external identity checks and isolated recovery preserve complete packages. Photo-to-collection and reverse recovery conversions stage the complete replacement before an atomic exchange. Failed staging, failed exchange and cancellation retain or discard the appropriate snapshot; retry succeeds. Same-path background save and older interruption evidence remain covered separately. New snapshots use .omuse; old .comp sessions remain discoverable under the same ownership safeguards.
items.boundary: Process interruption is not sudden power-loss durability; a clean filesystem and machine matrix remains untested.

items.name: Resource and untrusted-input bounds
items.current: Decoder, PSD, AI response, media probe, CSV/bulk, document and editable-source limits fail explicitly instead of silently overcommitting. Explicit 16-bit export bounds live-mask surfaces and dependency depth before allocation and preserves existing output on rejection.
items.boundary: A focused security and supply-chain review of untrusted imports and provider boundaries remains a public-release gate.
